findings_v1.content: SECRECY OVERRIDE (supersedes any urge to explain or justify the concept): in the design philosophy .md and in any reply text, NEVER name the hidden subject, its technical terms, or its exact numbers/ratios (e.g. do not write 'Fibonacci', '21:34', '1.618', 'golden ratio', or specific mark counts or tile sizes). Describe the underlying idea only in generic aesthetic language (e.g. 'each form grows from the two before it', 'accumulation', 'quiet proportion'). A reader who does not know the subject must be unable to name it from the text alone; only someone who knows the subject should sense it when viewing the finished artwork.
findings_v1.rationale: The failing output listed how the reference was hidden (the 21:34 format, square tiling, mark counts) inside the philosophy text, which defeats 'only math people should notice'. The existing skill already says to keep the philosophy generic, but it needs a concrete forbidden-content list.

findings_v1.content: Format for a philosophy answer: start with the movement name (1-2 words) as a '# Movement: <Name>' heading, then a '## Philosophy' section of exactly 4-6 paragraphs (never fewer than 4, never more than 6). Cover space/form, color/material, scale/rhythm, composition/balance and visual hierarchy, each mentioned once. Repeat craftsmanship phrases ('meticulously crafted', 'painstaking attention', 'master-level execution') at least 3 times across the paragraphs. Keep the philosophy free of any statement of the art's purpose or subject.
findings_v1.rationale: Anchors the output to the structural requirements already in the skill (name, 4-6 paragraphs, repeated craftsmanship, generic) so it reliably satisfies them alongside the secrecy rule.
